Eos Energy Enterprises Announces Preliminary Third Quarter 2026 Revenue Growth and Continued Gross Margin Improvement and Sets Conference Call Date PITTSBURGH, PA, October 19, 2026 — Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc. (NASDAQ: EOSE) (“Eos” or the “Company”), America’s leading innovator in designing, manufacturing, and providing zinc- based long-duration energy storage (LDES) systems sourced and manufactured in the United States, today announced preliminary financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Based on preliminary financial information, Eos currently expects:  Revenue of $82 to $83 million, representing approximately 19% to 21% sequential growth and approximately 169% to 172% year-over-year growth. Shipments increased approximately 23% quarter over quarter, supported by continued production scaling at the Company's second manufacturing line at its Thorn Hill facility. During the quarter, Line 2 contributed approximately 17% of total battery production and exited the quarter with first- pass yield aligned to Line 1 performance. The line continued to operate on a partial-shift schedule at Thorn Hill as the Company progressed the hiring, onboarding, and training of additional employees to support production growth and full-shift operations.  GAAP gross margin of (55)% to (53)%, representing an improvement of approximately 16 to 18 percentage points compared to the second quarter of 2026, driven by higher production volumes and lower conversion costs per unit. Eos achieved its eighth consecutive quarter of gross margin improvement. As the Company continues staffing and training employees to support additional shifts on Line 2 at Thorn Hill, Eos expects further margin expansion from higher production volumes, higher capacity utilization, consolidation into one footprint, and ongoing material cost-reduction initiatives.  Total cash, including restricted cash, was approximately $344 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $364 million as of June 30, 2026. Quarter-end cash was supported by approximately $114 million of operating cash inflows driven primarily by customer deposits, project milestone receipts, and tax credit collections, as well as an additional $87 million advance under the DOE loan facility. Capital expenditures totaled approximately $35 million, primarily related to completion of Line 2 automation.  Backlog of approximately $765 million as of September 30, 2026, representing approximately 3.2 GWh, after revenue recognized during the quarter and new orders booked. During the quarter, six purchase orders were received from six different customers, including a previously announced $100 million order under an existing capacity reservation agreement, which did not contribute to quarter-over-quarter backlog growth. Commercial traction continued across the defense, commercial & industrial (C&I), and data center markets. During the quarter, Eos announced key projects supporting the Golden Dome initiative for mission-critical defense applications and, alongside MN8, a project with Google, highlighting the growing demand for long-duration energy storage systems in data center applications.
The Company currently expects full-year 2026 revenue in the lower half of its $300 million to $350 million range. The current forecast reflects the addition of the final shift to bring Thorn Hill to 24- hour operation during the fourth quarter. Eos enters the fourth quarter with strong revenue visibility supported by customer commitments and projects in backlog. Following the manufacturing consolidation and achievement of full-scale operations, Thorn Hill will serve as the Company's manufacturing facility and is expected to have approximately 4 GWh of annual nameplate production capacity across its two production lines. “We delivered our highest revenue to date and improved gross margin by roughly 17 points as volume begins to ramp at Thorn Hill,” said Alessandro Lagi, Chief Financial Officer of Eos. “Consolidating into Thorn Hill is the right decision for the Company. It gives us one modern, higher throughput site, lowers our cost per unit, and puts us on a clear path to positive margins. We’re being disciplined about the transition in the fourth quarter and customer demand for American- made long-duration storage remains strong.” Conference Call Details The Company will report its full third quarter 2026 financial results before the U.S. market opens on November 5, 2026. A conference call to discuss its results will take place the same morning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. The live webcast of the earnings call will be available on the “Investor Relations” page of the Company’s website at Eos Investors or may be accessed using this link (Registration Link). To avoid delays, we encourage participants to join the conference call fifteen minutes ahead of the scheduled start time. The conference call replay will be available via webcast through Eos’ investor relations website for twelve months following the live presentation. The webcast replay will be available from approximately 11:30 a.m. Eastern Time on November 5, 2026, and can be accessed by visiting Eos Investors. About Eos Energy Enterprises Eos is accelerating the shift to American energy independence with positively ingenious solutions that transform how the world stores power. The Company’s BESS features the innovative Znyth™ technology, a proven chemistry with readily available non-precious earth components, that is the pre-eminent safe, non-flammable, secure, stable, and scalable alternative to conventional technology. The Company’s BESS is ideal for utility-scale, microgrid, commercial, and industrial long-duration energy storage applications (i.e., 4 to 16+ hours) and provides customers with significant operational flexibility to cost effectively address current and future increased grid demand and complexity. For more information about Eos (NASDAQ: EOSE), visit eose.com. Contacts Investors: ir@eose.com Media: media@eose.com Forward-Looking Statements and Important Information

Key Metrics Backlog. Our backlog represents the amount of revenue that we expect to realize from existing agreements with our customers for the sale of our battery energy storage systems and performance of services. The backlog is calculated by adding new orders in the current fiscal period to the backlog as of the end of the prior fiscal period and then subtracting the shipments in the current fiscal period. If the amount of an order is modified or cancelled, we adjust orders in the current period and our backlog accordingly, but do not retroactively adjust previously published backlogs. There is no comparable U.S. GAAP financial measure to backlog. We believe that the backlog is a useful indicator regarding the future revenue of our Company.
